req.title: Reject wrong method on /patch
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than PATCH on /patch.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /patch must accept PATCH and reject all other HTTP methods with 405. Tests cover: (1) positive - PATCH succeeds with 200 and correct JSON payload keys; (2) negative - GET, POST, PUT, DELETE each return exactly 405; (3) boundary - HEAD and OPTIONS (edge-case methods) also return 405; (4) decision-table covering all common wrong methods systematically; (5) BVA on the exact status code value 405 (not 404, not 406).

trace: get_dict() returns url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_patch_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.patch('/patch')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in data, f'Missing key: {key}'

test_patch_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload()

tests.name: test_all_wrong_methods_on_patch_return_exactly_405
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin app
Send GET, POST, PUT, DELETE requests to /patch
Assert each returns exactly 405 (not 404, not 406, not 400)
expected: All non-PATCH methods return exactly HTTP 405
Status code is not 406 (not a content negotiation error)
Status code is not 400 (not a bad request error)
trace: BVA: exact boundary of 405 vs adjacent codes 404 and 406
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_all_wrong_methods_on_patch_return_exactly_405():
    client = app.test_client()
    wrong_methods = [
        ('GET', client.get),
        ('POST', client.post),
        ('PUT', client.put),
        ('DELETE', client.delete),
    ]
    for method_name, method_fn in wrong_methods:
        r = method_fn('/patch')
        assert r.status_code == 405, f'{method_name} expected 405, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.status_code != 404, f'{method_name} got 404 (route missing?)'
        assert r.status_code != 406, f'{method_name} got 406 (wrong error type)'
        assert r.status_code != 400, f'{method_name} got 400 (wrong error type)'
        assert r.status_code != 200, f'{method_name} got 200 (should be rejected)'

test_all_wrong_methods_on_patch_return_exactly_405()

preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin app
Send PATCH request to /patch with JSON body
expected: Response JSON contains exactly the keys: url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
trace: view_patch calls get_dict with url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json as _json

def test_patch_response_payload_keys_are_exact():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.patch(
        '/patch',
        data=_json.dumps({'key': 'value'}),
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    expected_keys = {'url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'}
    assert set(body.keys()) == expected_keys
    assert body['json'] == {'key': 'value'}

test_patch_response_payload_keys_are_exact()

tests.name: test_status_code_boundary_404_vs_405_vs_406
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET to /patch (wrong method on existing route)
Assert status is exactly 405 (boundary between 404 and 406)
expected: Status code != 406 (not a media type error)
trace: BVA: 405 is the exact boundary value; 404 and 406 are adjacent incorrect values
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_status_code_boundary_404_vs_405_vs_406():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/patch')
    # Exact boundary: must be 405, not 404 (route missing) or 406 (content error)
    assert r.status_code == 405
    assert r.status_code - 1 == 404  # confirms we are at exactly 405
    assert r.status_code + 1 == 406  # confirms we are at exactly 405

test_status_code_boundary_404_vs_405_vs_406()
